minutes.headline: Sewer Commission agreed to hold a workshop with the town manager to draft a communications policy
minutes.summary: The meeting was mostly a dispute over how individual commissioners, especially the vice-chair, contact the DPW director, business manager and vendors such as Weston and Sampson. Members agreed to a workshop with the town manager and DPW director to draft a communications policy, and also covered town counsel access, legal billing, pump spare parts and the I&I task proposals. Only the 10/10 minutes were approved; the 10/31 minutes were tabled.

public_comment.topic: Objected to treating the Passios building kitchen grease trap as a chargeable commercial connection when it is a municipal building.
A member read a statement criticising emails and directives from an individual commissioner to the DPW director and vendors, and asked for communication to go through the full commission.
Another member objected to one member writing meeting summaries and sending them out before the commission had reviewed them.

what_happened.line: Members agreed to join a workshop with the town manager and DPW director to clarify roles and draft a communications policy.
The meeting was largely a dispute over how individual commissioners contact the DPW director, business manager and vendors; no recorded votes are listed.
The Weston and Sampson update and the spare parts list were deferred to the next agenda.
A member said sewer legal costs should be paid by users rather than through the town retainer, and wanted a mechanism in the next budget.
The 10/10 minutes were approved and the 10/31 minutes were tabled to the next meeting.

why_it_matters: Sewer costs are paid by users through the sewer enterprise fund, so who pays legal bills and how vendors are directed bear on sewer bills and on what taxes cover.
Until a communications policy exists, how vendor work such as pump parts and inflow and infiltration tasks is requested and approved remains unsettled.
